Guide

Build plugins for NextPluggable

A plugin is a folder in a GitHub repository. A site that runs NextPluggable installs it from its dashboard, straight from the repository at an exact commit. Nothing is published to npm, and the site is not rebuilt.

One plugin can add server-rendered pages that search engines index, HTTP endpoints, stored data, widgets in the site's layout, a settings form, and screens inside the dashboard.

Working with a coding agent? Give it this page as Markdown.

https://rohittp0.github.io/NextPluggable/build.md

#How a plugin reaches a site

  1. You write source in src/ and a manifest, plugin.json.
  2. nextpluggable-plugin build writes dist/: the bundles and dist/build.json, which records the manifest and a fingerprint of every file.
  3. You commit dist/ and push.
  4. The site's owner connects the repository under Sources in their dashboard and installs the plugin. The site downloads dist/ at that commit, checks every file against its fingerprint, and the plugin is live about a second later.
  5. When you push a new build, the dashboard offers it as an update.

#Requirements

  • Node.js 20.16 or newer.
  • A GitHub repository, public or private.
  • React knowledge. Plugin UI is React client components.

#1. Create the repository

Use this layout for a new repository. It holds any number of plugins.

acme-plugins/
  nextpluggable.json      lists the plugin folders
  package.json
  tsconfig.json
  plugin-env.d.ts         lets TypeScript accept CSS and image imports
  plugins/
    hello/
      plugin.json         the manifest
      src/client.tsx      React components: pages, widgets, dashboard screens
      src/server.ts       optional: page loaders and HTTP endpoints
      src/style.css       optional: imported from client.tsx
      dist/               build output. Commit it

nextpluggable.json names the repository and lists every plugin folder:

json
{
  "name": "Acme plugins",
  "description": "Plugins maintained by Acme.",
  "plugins": ["plugins/hello"]
}

package.json:

json
{
  "name": "acme-plugins",
  "private": true,
  "type": "module",
  "scripts": {
    "build": "nextpluggable-plugin build plugins/hello",
    "validate": "nextpluggable-plugin validate plugins/hello",
    "typecheck": "tsc --noEmit"
  }
}

When you add a plugin, add its folder to nextpluggable.json and to both scripts: nextpluggable-plugin build plugins/hello && nextpluggable-plugin build plugins/cart.

tsconfig.json:

json
{
  "compilerOptions": {
    "target": "ES2022",
    "lib": ["ES2023", "DOM", "DOM.Iterable"],
    "module": "ESNext",
    "moduleResolution": "Bundler",
    "jsx": "react-jsx",
    "strict": true,
    "noEmit": true,
    "skipLibCheck": true,
    "isolatedModules": true
  },
  "include": ["plugins/*/src", "plugin-env.d.ts"]
}

plugin-env.d.ts:

ts
// Asset imports understood by `nextpluggable-plugin build`.
declare module '*.css';
declare module '*.svg' {
  const url: string;
  export default url;
}
declare module '*.png' {
  const url: string;
  export default url;
}

.gitignore must ignore node_modules/ and must not ignore dist/.

A repository with exactly one plugin may instead keep plugin.json, src/ and dist/ at its root, with no nextpluggable.json. The build commands then take no folder.

Check: the files above exist, and dist appears nowhere in .gitignore.

#2. Install the SDK

bash
npm install --save-dev @nextpluggable/plugin@latest esbuild react @types/react typescript

@nextpluggable/plugin is the SDK and the build tool. esbuild does the bundling. react is needed for types and is never bundled into a plugin. Add @types/node if the server code uses Node built-ins.

Check: npx nextpluggable-plugin prints its usage.

#3. Write the manifest

plugins/hello/plugin.json says what the plugin adds. Everything the site's owner sees about the plugin comes from this file.

json
{
  "manifestVersion": 1,
  "id": "hello",
  "name": "Hello",
  "version": "1.0.0",
  "description": "A greeting page with a visitor counter, and a small badge on every page.",
  "author": "Acme",
  "icon": "👋",
  "category": "Examples",

  "pages": [
    { "id": "greeting", "path": "/hello", "component": "HelloPage", "title": "Hello" }
  ],
  "slots": [{ "slot": "body.end", "component": "HelloBadge" }],
  "admin": [{ "id": "stats", "title": "Stats", "component": "HelloStats" }],

  "permissions": ["storage"],
  "settings": [
    { "key": "greeting", "label": "Greeting", "type": "text", "default": "Hello there", "required": true },
    { "key": "showBadge", "label": "Show a badge on every page", "type": "toggle", "default": true },
    { "key": "accent", "label": "Accent colour", "type": "color", "placeholder": "Your site's colour", "help": "Leave empty to use your site's own colour." }
  ]
}

#Top-level fields

FieldRequiredRules
manifestVersionYesAlways 1
idYes3 to 50 characters: lowercase letters, digits and dashes, starting with a letter and not ending with a dash. Unique across everything a site installs. Changing it makes a different plugin
nameYesAt most 80 characters
versionYes1.2.3. Shown to the owner
descriptionAt most 500 characters. One or two sentences the owner reads before installing
author, homepage, categoryText
iconAn emoji, or the path of a .svg, .png, .webp or .jpg file inside the plugin folder, 32 kB at most. It is inlined at build time
entry{ "client": "…", "server": "…" } to use other entry files than src/client.* and src/server.*
pagesPages the plugin adds
slotsComponents to render in named places of the site's layout
adminScreens added as tabs on the plugin's page in the dashboard
settingsThe settings form
permissionsWhat the plugin does, shown to the owner before install: storage, email, fetch:<host> or fetch:*. Declare honestly. Sites display these today and will enforce them once plugins are sandboxed

#Pages

json
{ "id": "product", "path": "/shop/:slug", "component": "ProductPage", "title": "Product", "description": "One product." }
KeyRules
idA short identifier: letters, digits and underscores, starting with a letter. The server loader for the page is matched by it
pathThe default address. Starts with /, has no trailing slash, and cannot be / itself. :name matches one segment, and a final * matches the rest. Both arrive in params
componentThe name of a component exported from the client entry
titleShown in the dashboard, and the default <title>
descriptionOptional. Shown in the dashboard, and the default meta description
configurablePathOptional. false stops the owner changing the address
  • The owner can change the address of any page with a fixed path. Never hard-code your own addresses. Read them from usePlugin().paths in components and ctx.paths on the server.
  • The site's own routes always win over plugin pages, and two plugins cannot claim the same address. /api, /_next and the dashboard's addresses are reserved.
  • The server never sees the query string, because sites may cache plugin pages and share them between visitors. Put anything search engines should see in the address itself, such as /shop/page/:n, and read filters and searches in the browser with useQuery().

#Slots

json
{ "slot": "body.end", "component": "HelloBadge", "order": 10 }

A slot component receives no props. The conventional slot names are header.actions, footer and body.end. A site renders only the slots its developer placed in the layout, so a widget may not appear on every site. Lower order renders first.

#Dashboard screens

json
{ "id": "stats", "title": "Stats", "component": "HelloStats" }

Each entry is a tab on the plugin's page in the dashboard, shown only to the signed-in owner.

#Settings

Each entry becomes one field of a generated form. Labels and help text are read by a non-technical person, so write them in plain words.

typeFieldExtra keys
text, textarea, url, emailText inputs, validated accordinglyplaceholder
numberNumber inputmin, max, step
toggleOn/off switch
selectDropdownoptions: [{ "value", "label" }], required
colorColour picker, stored as #rrggbb
secretWrite-only field for API keys and the likeNo default allowed

Common keys: key (an identifier, like a page id), label, help, default, required, group (a section heading), serverOnly.

  • A default must match the type: a number for number, true or false for toggle, text for everything else.
  • secret values are encrypted at rest, reach server code only, and are never shown again in the dashboard.
  • "serverOnly": true keeps any other setting away from browsers.
  • A plugin with a required setting that has no value is installed paused, and switches on once the owner fills it in.
  • On update, values the owner already entered are kept for settings that still exist.

Check: npx nextpluggable-plugin validate plugins/hello prints ✓ Hello 1.0.0 — plugin.json is valid. On a mistake it lists every problem in words.

#4. Write the client entry

src/client.tsx exports every component the manifest names. They are ordinary React client components: hooks, state and effects all work.

tsx
// plugins/hello/src/client.tsx
import { useEffect, useState } from 'react';
import { Link, usePlugin, usePluginApi, usePluginConfig, type PageProps } from '@nextpluggable/plugin';
import './style.css';

interface Config {
  greeting: string;
  showBadge: boolean;
  /** Empty unless the owner chose a colour. The site's own colour applies then. */
  accent?: string;
}

const accent = (color?: string) => (color ? { ['--hello-accent' as string]: color } : undefined);

/** The page at /hello. `data` comes from the server loader. */
export function HelloPage({ data }: PageProps<{ visits: number }>) {
  const config = usePluginConfig<Config>();
  const api = usePluginApi();
  const [visits, setVisits] = useState(data.visits);

  // Counted in the browser: the server-rendered page may be cached and shared.
  useEffect(() => {
    api('/visits', { method: 'POST' })
      .then((res) => (res.ok ? res.json() : null))
      .then((body: { visits: number } | null) => body && setVisits(body.visits))
      .catch(() => {});
  }, [api]);

  return (
    <main className="hello" style={accent(config.accent)}>
      <h1>{config.greeting}</h1>
      <p className="hello-count">This page has been opened {visits} times.</p>
    </main>
  );
}

/** A widget for the `body.end` slot. Slot components receive no props. */
export function HelloBadge() {
  const config = usePluginConfig<Config>();
  const { paths } = usePlugin();
  if (!config.showBadge) return null;
  return (
    <Link href={paths.greeting ?? '/hello'} className="hello-badge" style={accent(config.accent)}>
      {config.greeting}
    </Link>
  );
}

/** A dashboard screen. Only the signed-in owner sees it. */
export function HelloStats() {
  const api = usePluginApi();
  const [visits, setVisits] = useState<number | null>(null);

  useEffect(() => {
    api('/visits')
      .then((res) => (res.ok ? res.json() : null))
      .then((body: { visits: number } | null) => setVisits(body?.visits ?? 0))
      .catch(() => setVisits(0));
  }, [api]);

  return <p className="hello-count">{visits === null ? 'Loading…' : `${visits} visits so far.`}</p>;
}

What @nextpluggable/plugin provides:

ExportWhat it gives you
usePluginConfig<T>()The owner's settings, minus secrets and server-only values
usePlugin(){ id, version, apiBase, paths, page }. paths maps your page ids to their current addresses. On a page, page is { id, path, params }
usePluginApi()api(path, init): a fetch bound to your plugin's endpoints. Pass { json } to send a JSON body
useNavigation(){ pathname, push, replace, back } from the site's router
useQuery()The query string as URLSearchParams. Browser-only: empty in the server-rendered HTML and on the first render, then it fills in
LinkA client-side navigation link. Props: href, children, className, style, title and aria-label
PageProps<Data>Props of a page component: data from the server loader and params from the address

Rules for client code:

  • react, react-dom and @nextpluggable/plugin come from the site and are not bundled. That is why plugin bundles are small and why a plugin shares the site's router. Everything else you import is bundled into the plugin.
  • No Next.js imports. next/link, next/image, next/navigation, server components and server actions are not available. Use Link, useNavigation() and plain <img>.
  • Components are rendered on the server first, then hydrated. Do not read window, document or localStorage while rendering. Do it in an effect. A component that throws on the server is left out of the page and rendered in the browser instead, so its content is missing from the HTML search engines read.
  • Images and fonts imported from the client entry (.svg, .png, .jpg, .gif, .webp, .woff2) are inlined as data URLs. Keep them small, or link to hosted files.

Check: every component named in plugin.json is exported from the client entry.

#5. Write the server entry

src/server.ts is optional. It runs on the site's server and uses the web-standard Request and Response.

ts
// plugins/hello/src/server.ts
import { adminOnly, definePluginServer, json } from '@nextpluggable/plugin/server';

interface Config {
  greeting: string;
}

export default definePluginServer<Config>({
  // Runs before a page renders: fetch data and describe the page to search engines.
  pages: {
    greeting: async ({ config, storage, site, path }) => ({
      data: { visits: (await storage.get<number>('visits')) ?? 0 },
      metadata: { title: config.greeting, description: 'A friendly greeting.' },
      jsonLd: { '@context': 'https://schema.org', '@type': 'WebPage', name: config.greeting, url: site.url + path },
    }),
  },

  // HTTP endpoints under the plugin's own base address.
  api: {
    'POST /visits': async ({ storage }) => {
      const visits = ((await storage.get<number>('visits')) ?? 0) + 1;
      await storage.set('visits', visits);
      return json({ visits });
    },
    'GET /visits': adminOnly(async ({ storage }) => json({ visits: (await storage.get<number>('visits')) ?? 0 })),
  },

  onInstall: async ({ storage }) => storage.set('visits', 0),
});

The entry must export default definePluginServer({ … }).

#Context

Every function receives a context object:

KeyMeaning
configAll settings, including secrets and server-only values
storageThe plugin's private key-value store: get(key), set(key, value), delete(key), list(prefix). Values are JSON, 1 MB each at most. No other plugin can read it
site.urlThe site's public address, such as https://example.com
pathsCurrent addresses of the plugin's pages, by page id
pluginIdThe plugin's id
log(...)Writes to the server log, tagged with the plugin id
path, paramsPage loaders: the requested address and its parameters
request, path, params, adminEndpoints: the Request, the path below the plugin's base, its parameters, and the signed-in dashboard user or null

#Page loaders

pages is keyed by page id. A loader returns any of:

KeyMeaning
dataPassed to the page component as data. Must be JSON-serialisable
metadata{ title, description, canonical, image, noindex }
jsonLdschema.org structured data: an object or a list of objects
notFound: trueRespond with the site's 404 page
redirect: '/somewhere'Redirect to another address

A site may cache plugin pages. Write loaders as if their result is shared by every visitor and kept for a while. Cached pages are refreshed whenever the owner changes anything in the dashboard, and whenever the owner changes data through one of your endpoints. Data changed by visitors does not refresh them, so load fast-changing or per-visitor content from the browser, as the example does with its counter.

#Endpoints

api is keyed by "METHOD /path". The methods are GET, POST, PUT, PATCH and DELETE, and a path may hold :name parameters: 'DELETE /items/:id'. A handler returns a Response.

  • Endpoints are public unless wrapped in adminOnly. That is what makes form posts and third-party webhooks possible, so validate everything a visitor sends.
  • Call your endpoints from components with usePluginApi(). It knows the base address and adds the header that marks the request as coming from the site's own pages.
  • For requests that change data, admin is only set when the call came through usePluginApi() from the site itself, so another website cannot act as the signed-in owner.
  • Helpers from @nextpluggable/plugin/server: json(body, status?, headers?) builds a JSON response, and readJson<T>(request, maxBytes?) reads a JSON body, returning null when it is missing, malformed or too large.

#Lifecycle

onInstall runs once, on first install, not on updates. If it throws, or if the server entry throws while loading, the install is cancelled and the owner is told the plugin failed to start. onUninstall runs before removal. Stored data is kept unless the owner asks for it to be deleted.

Rules for server code:

  • Do no work when the file loads. The entry is loaded during the build and again on install. Top-level code that throws, or that needs a network or a database, breaks both. Do the work inside loaders, handlers and onInstall.
  • Only Node built-ins exist at runtime. Any package you import is bundled into dist/server.js. Packages that need native binaries or their own files on disk will not work.
  • No query string in loaders. Use address parameters.

Check: every key under pages matches a page id in plugin.json, and every key under api looks like GET /path.

#6. Style it

Import CSS from the client entry. It is bundled into dist/style.css and loaded with your components.

css
/* plugins/hello/src/style.css */
.hello,
.hello-badge {
  /* The site's brand colour, unless the owner picked one in the settings. */
  --hello-accent: var(--np-accent, #4f46e5);
}
.hello {
  max-width: 40rem;
  margin: 0 auto;
  padding: 3rem 1rem;
  color: var(--np-text, #0f172a);
}
.hello h1 {
  color: var(--hello-accent);
}
.hello-count {
  color: var(--np-muted, #5b6474);
}
.hello-badge {
  position: fixed;
  right: 1rem;
  bottom: 1rem;
  padding: 0.5rem 0.9rem;
  border-radius: 999px;
  background: var(--hello-accent);
  color: #fff;
  text-decoration: none;
}

Take your colours from the site. A site describes its look with five CSS custom properties. Read them, always with a fallback, because a site may set none of them:

PropertyUse it for
--np-accentThe site's brand colour: buttons, links, highlights
--np-textBody text
--np-mutedSecondary text
--np-borderLines and input borders
--np-surfaceThe background of cards and inputs
  • Do not give a colour setting a default. Leave it empty, fall back to --np-accent in CSS, and apply the owner's value only when there is one, as the example does. A default would override every site's own colour.
  • Inherit the site's fonts. Do not set font-family.
  • There is no style isolation. Prefix every class with something of your own (.hello-…). Never style bare elements such as h1 or button outside your own root class.
  • Do not render a header or footer of your own. The site puts its own around your page.
  • The dashboard sets --np-text, --np-muted, --np-border and --np-surface too, so dashboard screens match it.

#7. Build and commit

bash
npm run build
npm run typecheck

The build writes, per plugin:

FileContents
dist/client.jsThe components, minified
dist/server.jsLoaders and endpoints, self-contained
dist/style.cssAny CSS the client entry imports
dist/build.jsonThe manifest, the icon, and a fingerprint of every file

It stops with a plain message when the manifest names a component the client entry does not export, when the server entry has a loader for a page that does not exist, or when an endpoint key is malformed. --no-minify keeps the client bundle readable.

Commit dist/ together with the source change that produced it. Sites install from the repository at an exact commit and refuse any file that does not match the fingerprint in build.json. Builds are reproducible: rebuilding without changes leaves dist/ untouched.

Sites accept bundles up to 3 MB for client.js, 5 MB for server.js and 1 MB for style.css.

Check: after npm run build, git status shows dist/ changes only if the source or manifest changed. Commit them.

#8. Try it on a site

A site in development accepts a folder on the same machine as a source.

  1. Run a site that has NextPluggable (integration guide) with next dev.
  2. Open /admin/plugins, sign in, and go to Sources.
  3. Enter the absolute path of the repository folder and connect it.
  4. Under Add plugins, install the plugin. Open its page.
  5. After each rebuild, press Check for updates, then Update.

Check these before calling the plugin finished:

  • The page's content is in the HTML the server sends (curl the address). That is what search engines read.
  • The settings form makes sense to someone who has never seen the code.
  • The page takes on the site's colours and font, and sits between the site's own header and footer.
  • The page still works after the owner changes its address in the dashboard.
  • Nothing in the browser console reports a hydration mismatch.

#9. Publish and update

Push the repository to GitHub. The site's owner connects it under Sources by pasting its address. All of these forms work:

AddressFollows
https://github.com/acme/acme-plugins or acme/acme-pluginsThe default branch
https://github.com/acme/acme-plugins/tree/stableThe branch or tag stable
https://github.com/acme/acme-plugins/tree/main/packages/pluginsA subfolder that holds nextpluggable.json or a single plugin

For a private repository, the owner ticks This repository is private and pastes a read-only access token. The dashboard walks them through creating one.

To release an update:

  1. Change the source.
  2. Raise version in plugin.json.
  3. Run npm run build.
  4. Commit source and dist/ together, and push.

The owner's dashboard offers the update. Their settings and the plugin's stored data are kept.

Never change after release: the plugin id (it becomes a different plugin), a page id (the owner's chosen address is lost), or a setting key (the owner's value is lost).

To have CI refuse a stale dist/:

yaml
# .github/workflows/check.yml
name: Check
on: [push, pull_request]
jobs:
  check:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          node-version: 24
      - run: npm ci
      - run: npm run typecheck
      - run: npm run build
      - name: dist/ must match the source
        run: test -z "$(git status --porcelain)" || (git status --short && exit 1)

#Add this to CLAUDE.md

Put this block in the CLAUDE.md at the root of the plugin repository. Adjust the layout lines if the repository holds a single plugin at its root.

markdown
## NextPluggable plugins

This repository is a NextPluggable plugin source. Sites install plugins straight from
it at an exact commit, using the built files in each plugin's `dist/`.
Full guide: https://rohittp0.github.io/NextPluggable/build.md
Read it before creating a plugin or changing a manifest.

### Layout

- `nextpluggable.json` lists every plugin folder. A new plugin must be added to it and
  to the `build` and `validate` scripts in `package.json`.
- `plugins/<id>/plugin.json` is the manifest.
- `plugins/<id>/src/client.tsx` exports the React components the manifest names.
- `plugins/<id>/src/server.ts` (optional) default-exports
  `definePluginServer({ pages, api })`.
- `plugins/<id>/dist/` is build output.

### Commands

- `npm run build` rebuilds every plugin's `dist/`.
- `npm run typecheck` type-checks the sources.
- `npm run validate` checks the manifests without building.

### Rules

- After any change under `plugins/<id>/`, source or `plugin.json`, run the build and
  commit `dist/` in the same commit. Never edit `dist/` by hand and never add it to
  `.gitignore`: sites refuse files that do not match `dist/build.json`.
- Raise `version` in `plugin.json` with every change that should reach sites.
- Never change a plugin `id`, a page `id` or a setting `key` after release. Sites key
  installs, page addresses and saved settings on them.
- Client code imports only `react`, `react-dom`, `@nextpluggable/plugin` and packages
  that can be bundled. No `next/*` imports, server components or server actions.
- Components render on the server first. Do not touch `window`, `document` or
  `localStorage` while rendering; use an effect.
- Do not hard-code this plugin's page addresses or endpoint URLs. Use
  `usePlugin().paths`, `ctx.paths` and `usePluginApi()`.
- Server code never sees the query string. Use address parameters (`/shop/:slug`) and
  read filters in the browser with `useQuery()`.
- Endpoints are public unless wrapped in `adminOnly`. Validate all input.
- The server entry must do no work and must not throw when it loads. It is loaded
  during the build and on install.
- Prefix every CSS class with the plugin's own prefix. There is no style isolation.
- Take colours from the site: read `--np-accent`, `--np-text`, `--np-muted`,
  `--np-border` and `--np-surface`, each with a fallback. Never give a colour setting
  a default, never set `font-family`, and never render a header or footer.
- Settings labels and help text are read by non-technical site owners. Use plain words.

#Troubleshooting

Message or symptomCauseFix
Invalid plugin manifest: followed by a listplugin.json breaks a rule from step 3Fix each listed item
plugin.json refers to component "X", but the client entry does not export itA name in the manifest has no matching exportExport it from src/client.tsx, or fix the name
The server entry must export default definePluginServer({ ... })No default exportAdd it
The server entry has a loader for page "x", which plugin.json does not declareA key under pages matches no page idMake them match
API route "…" must look like "GET /path"A malformed endpoint keyUse one of the five methods, a space, then a path starting with /
The server entry throws when loadedTop-level code that failsMove the work into a loader, a handler or onInstall
Cannot require "x": server bundles may only use Node built-ins at runtimeA package was left out of the bundleImport it normally so it is bundled, or drop it
Building plugins needs esbuildesbuild is not installednpm install --save-dev esbuild
The dashboard says the source "does not look like a plugin source"No nextpluggable.json and no built plugin at the top levelAdd the index file, or build and commit dist/
"This plugin has not been built yet"dist/build.json is missing for a listed folderBuild and commit
"This plugin failed its integrity check"dist/ was edited by hand, or is staleRebuild and commit dist/ unchanged
The page appears, then its content flickers or the console reports a hydration mismatchThe first render differs between server and browserRender the same output first; change it in an effect
A widget does not appear on a siteThe site's layout has no slot with that nameAsk the site's developer to add it, or use body.end
usePluginConfig() lacks a valueThe setting is secret or serverOnlyRead it in server code and pass on only what the browser may see

#Done when

  • npm run build and npm run typecheck pass.
  • dist/ is committed and matches the source.
  • The plugin installs on a site from the repository, and its page, widgets and settings work.
  • The page's content is in the server-rendered HTML.
  • CLAUDE.md holds the block above.

The two reference plugins are worth reading: EMI Calculator, a page with settings only, and Enquiry Form, with a page, endpoints, stored data, a layout widget, a dashboard screen and a secret setting.

GitHub npm llms.txt Why it is built this way
